A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CodecSep and support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. The revised title and substantial reorganization do not obscure the correspondence between experiments.

before.justification: v4 reports original separation experiments across six benchmarks, architectural and reconstruction analyses, compute measurements, and a listening study with 20 participants.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and adds raw-audio baseline evaluations, codec-only reconstruction measurements, and a qualitative latent-space analysis.

M1.justification: The frozen DAC/CLAP pipeline, latent masking, and training objective remain. However, v4 Section 3.2 describes query-generated FiLM scales and biases and a single convolutional output head; v5 Section 3.2.3 specifies fixed unit scales and a two-convolution head. The PDFs do not resolve whether these represent implementation changes or corrections and elaborations of the earlier description.

E1.justification: The same six datasets, source categories, transfer directions, prompt regimes, and bandwidth settings are retained. v5 Table 3 adds native uncompressed-input evaluations for non-codec baselines, extending the tested input conditions without adding a corpus or application task.

E2.justification: v5 Table 7 introduces a DAC-only oracle reconstruction reference against CodecSep. The separator baseline families otherwise remain unchanged: Bimodal is renamed BiModalSS, and the masker ablation moves from v4 Table 1 to v5 Table 6 rather than becoming a new comparator.

E3.justification: v5 adds raw-audio training/evaluation protocols for non-codec baselines and a codec-only control that independently reconstructs reference mixtures and stems without a separator. It also introduces the latent-inspection procedure for clip 1590. The existing dataset splits, main training budget, metrics, and compute-benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds analyses of preprocessing effects, codec distortion versus separation error, and source-dependent latent structure and mask behavior through Table 3, Table 7, and Figure 3. Existing prompt, architectural, bandwidth, transfer, and reconstruction studies are retained, although several move between the appendices and main text.

E5.justification: Beyond v4's means and standard deviations, v5 reports paired gains, 95% confidence intervals, paired t-tests, and Wilcoxon tests across five benchmarks and the listening study. Listening-study inference uses per-clip means over the existing 20 clips. These are new statistical reporting practices, not evidence of additional training runs or an enlarged listening study.

E6.justification: v5 adds raw-audio baseline scores, DAC-only reconstruction results, statistical result entries, and the finding that the illustrated masks vary predominantly across channels. For example, the new DAC reference reports music/speech/SFX SI-SDR of 6.8/7.4/1.8 dB. Existing CodecSep separation scores, including 1.2/10.0/0.9 dB in Table 1, are retained; the additions do not establish improved same-setting model performance.

T1.justification: v5 introduces the explicit latent-residual diagnostic |Z − (Zspeech + Zmusic + ZSFX)/3| in Equation 13. Most other mathematical material restates the existing masking, loss, and codec pathways. No theorem or proof is added, and the residual analysis explicitly does not establish linear compositionality or exact disentanglement.

C1.justification: v5 elevates source-dependent latent organization and predominantly channel-wise masking into explicit central contributions, and presents the deployment pathway as a broader blueprint for codec-native processing. It also narrows v4's on-device positioning and removes the abstract's blanket matching-or-exceeding claim about fixed-stem baselines.

C2.justification: v5 substantially qualifies interpretations of generic prompting, AudioCaps transfer, reconstruction fidelity, bandwidth mismatch, and raw-audio efficiency. It adds explanations of codec versus separator distortion and channel-overlap leakage, and explicitly acknowledges that mobile or embedded deployment remains unvalidated. These are substantive qualifications beyond the retained limitations.

D1.justification: v5 documents codec-to-transformer projections, a single-linear-layer query network, post-LN FiLM placement, and initialization details more explicitly. The main hyperparameters and hardware information remain unchanged. v4's explicit supplementary-code statement is omitted; this changes the disclosure but does not establish that code availability changed.

R1.justification: v5 adds Glorot and Bengio (2010) for initialization and Peebles and Xie (2023) when contrasting FiLM with AdaLN-style generative conditioning. The related-work survey and claimed novelty relative to AudioSep, CodecFormer, and SDCodec are otherwise substantially retained.

P1.justification: v5 extensively rewrites the abstract, contribution statement, results discussion, conclusion, and Appendix B. It reorganizes the method into explicit subsections, adopts question-based experimental discussions, and creates separate limitations, future-work, broader-impact, and LLM-usage sections. This exceeds routine editing or expansion from new experiments alone.

P2.justification: v5 changes the document typography, title/author layout, headers, and overall page layout. It adds the eight-panel latent visualization and raw-audio/oracle tables, turns existing listening scores into a table, expands tables with statistical blocks, and relocates existing ablation, paraphrase, and bandwidth material.

improvement.justification: The added raw-audio and codec-only controls, statistical reporting, and more careful deployment and performance qualifications improve transparency. However, new inconsistencies limit the gain: Table 2 reports a 2.4 dB Clotho-v2 gain although its displayed means differ by 2.6 dB, and the raw-audio discussion overstates CodecSep's AudioCaps ranking in Tables 2–3. The revision provides useful additional evidence without fully reliable reporting.
